cost_lines.name: Food cost / COGS (raw material incl. factory transfers)
cost_lines.unit: % of net food sales (ex-GST, after restaurant-funded discounts)
cost_lines.notes: Indian restaurant target band 28-35%; QSR/cloud kitchen ~28-30%; above 38% is a red flag; gap >3 pts between theoretical and actual food cost signals waste/theft. Meat-heavy kebab/shawarma menus sit at upper end (32-36% is my estimate). Listed QSR gross margins 67-75% imply food+packaging 25-33%. Compute on NET sales after discounts, otherwise aggregator margins are overstated.

cost_lines.name: Delivery packaging (containers, foil, butter paper, bags, cutlery, stickers)
cost_lines.notes: Sources: Rs 8-22/order (Rs 15 in worked example); Rs 15-25/order; or 5-8% of order value for cloud kitchens. Rolls/shawarma at low end, biryani/kebab platters at high end.

cost_lines.name: In-store takeaway packaging
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION (no source found) - wrap + bag only; low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Zomato commission (base)
cost_lines.unit: % of Zomato order value (net of restaurant discount; ex customer GST)
cost_lines.notes: Negotiated per brand/city. 18% GST is charged on top (non-creditable for 5% restaurants) so effective ~21-33%. One secondary source claims Zomato computes on subtotal+packaging ex-GST while Swiggy includes GST in base - unverified, low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Swiggy commission (base)
cost_lines.notes: Ranges quoted: 17-25% (MenuManager), 18-28% (SpiceAdvisors), 15-30% (Petpooja blog snippet). Plus 18% GST.

cost_lines.name: Payment gateway / collection fee (aggregators)
cost_lines.notes: Shown as separate deduction line in payout statements; 18% GST on top.

cost_lines.name: GST @18% on aggregator commission, PG fee and ads (non-creditable)
cost_lines.unit: % of aggregator fees (approx 4.5-6% of channel sales)
cost_lines.notes: Becomes a pure cost because restaurant is on 5% GST without ITC.

cost_lines.name: Aggregator ads / visibility (Zomato Ads, Swiggy Ads CPC)
cost_lines.notes: Active bidders spend 4-9% of aggregator revenue. Minimum budgets ~Rs 400/day (Zomato) and ~Rs 500/day (Swiggy). CPC Rs 3-18; cost-per-order for QSR & biryani Rs 40-65; ROAS target 4-6x. Deducted from weekly payout. NRAI members have alleged unapproved ad/discount deductions (useful 'exceptions' storyline).

cost_lines.name: Restaurant-funded discounts on aggregators
cost_lines.notes: Worked monthly example in source shows 17.5% of menu GMV for a promo-heavy brand (e.g. Rs 100 off above Rs 399). Healthy net realisation after discount+commission+PG+ads+packaging = 52-62% of menu price; below 50% structurally loss-making. Typical 10% is my mid-case.

cost_lines.name: Customer complaint refunds / cancellation adjustments
cost_lines.notes: Line item exists in settlement reports (source); magnitude is an ASSUMPTION, low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Rent (see area_rents for per-sq-ft by locality)
cost_lines.notes: Low = Kalyan ~300 sq ft @ Rs 100; typical = Andheri W ~400 sq ft @ Rs 350; high = Bandra W ~500 sq ft @ Rs 700. Benchmarks: rent 8-15% of sales, healthy 10-12%, premium locations 15-20%. Deposit 3-6 months (often more in Mumbai); typical escalation ~5% p.a. (general practice, unsourced).

cost_lines.name: GST on commercial rent (non-creditable)
cost_lines.notes: Forward charge if landlord registered; RCM if landlord unregistered. Either way no ITC for a 5% restaurant so it is a P&L cost.

cost_lines.name: CAM / society maintenance and property-tax pass-through
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - no source found for high-street shops; malls/food courts are much higher per sq ft. Low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Electricity tariff - Mumbai (Adani/Tata Power/BEST) LT-II(a) Commercial up to 20 kW
cost_lines.unit: INR/kWh (energy+wheeling) plus fixed Rs 475/month, before duty/ToSE/FAC
cost_lines.notes: MERC MYT orders 28-Mar-2025. AEML: FY25-26 8.65 (5.72+2.93), FY26-27 7.98 (5.70+2.28). Tata Power: FY25-26 8.68 (5.92+2.76), FY26-27 8.00 (5.60+2.40). BEST: FY25-26 8.65 (6.55+2.10), FY26-27 7.99 (6.17+1.82). Fixed charge Rs 475/month all three. Above 20 kW: Rs 300/kVA demand + ~7.65-7.70/kVAh. Add electricity duty (21% commercial per secondary sources; one site says 16% - conflict, medium confidence) + Tax on Sale of Electricity 34.04 paise/unit in Mumbai + FAC. All-in approx Rs 10-10.5/kWh in FY26-27. No GST on electricity.

cost_lines.name: Electricity tariff - MSEDCL (Kalyan, Pune) LT-II(A) Non-Residential 0-20 kW
cost_lines.unit: INR/kWh (energy+wheeling) plus fixed Rs 520-540/month, before duty/ToSE/FAC
cost_lines.notes: MERC review order Case 75 of 2025 (superseded the March-2025 order which had shown 7.84): FY25-26 from 1-Jul-2025 = 8.90+1.47 = 10.37, fixed Rs 520; FY26-27 = 8.51+1.60 = 10.11, fixed Rs 540. 20-50 kW: Rs 550/kVA + 13.92/kVAh (FY26-27). ToSE 19.04 paise/unit in MSEDCL city areas (a ToSE revision circular dated 15-Apr-2026 exists - not read). All-in approx Rs 12-12.7/kWh. So Kalyan/Pune power is ~20% dearer per unit than Mumbai city.

cost_lines.name: Electricity - typical monthly bill, 300-500 sq ft QSR
cost_lines.notes: DERIVED: assumes 1,800-4,500 kWh/month (AC, exhaust, 2-3 freezers, visi-cooler, electric shawarma/grill optional) x all-in Rs 10-12.5/kWh. kWh is my assumption; tariff is sourced. Utilities benchmark 3-5% of sales (warning >7%).

cost_lines.name: Electricity tariff - factory / central kitchen on LT-III Industrial (AEML)
cost_lines.notes: AEML LT-III(a) up to 20 kW: 8.53 (FY25-26), 7.83 (FY26-27), fixed Rs 475/month; LT-III(b) >20 kW: Rs 400/kVA + 8.27 (FY25-26) / 7.65 (FY26-27) per kVAh. Only applies if the factory has an industrial connection; cold rooms/blast chillers make factory power a major line.

cost_lines.name: Commercial LPG 19 kg cylinder - Mumbai
cost_lines.notes: Mumbai price history: 2025 ranged 1,531.5 (Sep/Dec-25) to 1,756 (Jan-25); Jan-26 1,642.5; Feb-26 1,692; Mar-26 1,836; Apr-26 2,031; May-26 3,024; Jun-26 3,067.5; Aug-26 2,691.5; Sep-26 ~2,701. 2026 spike attributed to West Asia crisis. Strong storyline: gas cost per outlet up ~70% YoY. Commercial LPG carries 18% GST (non-creditable; general knowledge).

cost_lines.name: LPG - typical monthly spend per outlet
cost_lines.notes: DERIVED: assumes 6-15 cylinders/month for gas tandoor/griller + shawarma burners (assumption); at 2025 prices the same volume was ~Rs 10,000-25,000.

cost_lines.name: PNG commercial (Mahanagar Gas) alternative to LPG
cost_lines.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: Rs 60/SCM commercial from a secondary price-tracker page labelled 2025; likely higher now - MGL raised domestic PNG to Rs 53/SCM on 1-Sep-2026 citing costly spot RLNG. MGL does not publish commercial slabs on the pages I could reach.

cost_lines.name: Charcoal for tandoor/sigri
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - no price source found (search budget exhausted). Roughly 8-15 kg/day at Rs 40-60/kg. Low confidence; zero if outlet only finishes factory-made kebabs on gas/electric grill.

cost_lines.name: Water
cost_lines.notes: BMC commercial/industrial water charge Rs 50 per 1,000 litres (vs Rs 6 residential); 8% hike proposed but not implemented as of 2025. Volume (1-2 kL/day) is my assumption; often bundled in society maintenance or bought by tanker.

cost_lines.name: Outlet payroll (gross wages, 8-12 staff)
cost_lines.notes: Built from role table in staffing. Floor is Maharashtra minimum wage for Hotels & Restaurants, Zone I, 1-Jul-2026 to 31-Dec-2026: unskilled 14,676; semi-skilled 15,176; skilled 15,876 (basic + special allowance 8,176). Labour benchmarks: 18-25% / 20-30% of sales for restaurants generally; QSR with commissary can run 12-18% (my estimate).

cost_lines.name: EPF employer contribution (12% + ~1% EDLI/admin)
cost_lines.unit: % of PF wages (basic+DA, statutory ceiling Rs 15,000)
cost_lines.notes: Max ~Rs 1,950/employee/month at ceiling. New uniform wage definition (Labour Codes, from Nov/Dec 2025) requires wages to be at least 50% of gross, widening the PF/ESI base. 1% EDLI+admin split is general knowledge.

cost_lines.name: ESIC employer contribution
cost_lines.unit: % of gross wages for employees earning up to Rs 21,000/month
cost_lines.notes: Employee share 0.75%. Most outlet staff fall under the Rs 21,000 ceiling.

cost_lines.name: Statutory bonus + gratuity accrual
cost_lines.notes: General knowledge (Payment of Bonus Act min 8.33%; gratuity ~4.81%) - no source fetched; usually paid at Diwali, so show a bonus spike in Oct/Nov.

cost_lines.name: Staff meals
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - Rs 60-100 per staff per day for 8-10 staff. Common practice in Mumbai kitchens; no source. Low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Staff accommodation (shared room for migrant kitchen staff)
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - common practice, no source. Often one shared flat serves 2 nearby outlets. Low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Housekeeping and kitchen consumables (tissue paper, cleaning chemicals, gloves, hairnets, foil, garbage bags)
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION ~0.7-1.2% of sales; no specific source. Sits inside the 3-5% 'miscellaneous' benchmark.

cost_lines.name: Local / brand marketing (non-aggregator: social, flyers, influencer, own-app offers)
cost_lines.notes: Total marketing benchmark 2-5% of revenue (warning >8%); aggregator ads are shown separately above.

cost_lines.name: Repairs and maintenance (equipment, refrigeration, exhaust, plumbing, electrical)
cost_lines.notes: Benchmark 1-2% of revenue; warning above 4%. Make it lumpy in mock data (e.g. a compressor failure month).

cost_lines.name: Pest control (monthly service, commercial kitchen)
cost_lines.notes: Mumbai provider quotes commercial-kitchen monthly service from Rs 2,000/month (monthly needed due to humidity); AMC billing gives 25-40% saving vs one-off. 18% GST non-creditable.

cost_lines.name: Waste disposal (wet waste pickup, used cooking oil, grease trap cleaning)
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - no source found. Low confidence.

cost_lines.name: POS subscription (Petpooja) per outlet
cost_lines.notes: Petpooja does not publish prices. User-reported: ~Rs 10,000 first year / Rs 7,500 renewal for base billing; tiers roughly Rs 10k/20k/40k per year; with inventory, KDS, online-ordering integration Rs 25-40k/year. A competitor blog (DineOpen) claims Rs 36k-1.44 lakh/year - treat as outlier/biased. Hardware one-time Rs 15-50k.

cost_lines.name: Internet + phone
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - broadband + backup SIM/dongle for aggregator tablets; no source.

cost_lines.name: Card / UPI MDR on in-store (Petpooja) sales
cost_lines.notes: UPI P2M has been zero-MDR; a new regime effective 15-Oct-2026 levies 0.4% only on UPI P2M transactions above Rs 2,000 (capped Rs 300) - QSR tickets are below that so UPI stays ~free. Debit card up to 0.9%; credit card 1.5-2.5%. Blended rate depends on card share (assume 10-20% cards).

cost_lines.name: FSSAI licence (per outlet)
cost_lines.notes: State licence Rs 2,000-5,000/year. Secondary sources say thresholds were revised from 1-Apr-2026 (state licence for turnover Rs 1.5-50 crore at Rs 5,000/year; licences now perpetual with annual fee + annual return). Not verified on FoSCoS primary page - medium confidence. Factory needs its own (manufacturing) licence.

cost_lines.name: Other licences and renewals (Shops & Establishment, BMC health licence u/s 394, trade licence, fire NOC/compliance, signage, weights & measures) incl. consultant fees
cost_lines.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE - BMC fee schedule PDF exists but amounts not extracted; one source puts fire NOC fee ~Rs 2,000. BMC health licence can be issued for up to 5 years. Treat as a lumpy annual/renewal cost.

cost_lines.name: Music licence (PPL / IPRS / Novex) - only if music is played
cost_lines.notes: UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION - could not research tariffs (search budget exhausted). Suggest showing as zero for takeaway-format outlets or omitting.

cost_lines.name: Insurance (fire, burglary, equipment, public liability, cash-in-transit)
cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - no source found. Low confidence.

cost_lines.name: Petty cash / miscellaneous (local conveyance, tips, small purchases, printing)
cost_lines.notes: Benchmark: miscellaneous 3-5% of revenue in total (warning >7%) - this line plus consumables, licences, insurance should stay inside that.

cost_lines.name: Depreciation - kitchen equipment and fit-out
cost_lines.notes: DERIVED from capex: small QSR (200-400 sq ft) interiors Rs 2-4 lakh + equipment Rs 2-4 lakh + POS/signage ~Rs 0.4-1.1 lakh; medium (400-800 sq ft) interiors Rs 5-10 lakh + equipment Rs 4-8 lakh. Depreciate over ~5 years (lease term) - my assumption. Capitalise GST since no ITC. Shawarma machine Rs 22,500-29,700 (IndiaMART, Dec-2025). Total project cost incl. deposit and working capital Rs 10-20 lakh small / Rs 20-40 lakh medium; break-even 8-14 months.

cost_lines.notes: ASSUMPTION - no source found. Pune outlets (if served from a Mumbai factory) would cost materially more; consider whether Pune has its own prep kitchen.

benchmarks.value: Rs 15 L menu sales (60% aggregator): discounts ~0.9-1.1 L -> net ~13.9-14.1 L; food 33% ~4.6 L; packaging ~0.55 L; aggregator commission+PG+GST+ads ~2.9 L; rent 1.4 L + GST 0.25 L; utilities ~0.77 L; people ~2.7 L; other ~1.0 L -> roughly break-even. demand_patterns: Time of day: dinner is the peak window - Swiggy 2025 data shows dinner orders ~32% higher than lunch; the 3-7 pm snack window is dominated by burgers, rolls and pizzas; midnight-2 am ordering is growing, led by chicken burgers and biryani. Suggested mock split for a kebab/shawarma QSR (assumption): lunch 12-3 pm ~20-25%, snack 4-7 pm ~15%, dinner 7-11 pm ~45-50%, late night 11 pm-1:30 am ~10-15%. Fort outlet should be lunch-heavy on weekdays and weak on Sundays.

Day of week: platforms confirm weekends, festivals, sporting events and late nights carry materially higher volumes, but I found no published weekday/weekend ratio. Assumption for mock: Mon-Thu = 1.0, Fri ~1.15, Sat ~1.35, Sun ~1.3. In Hindu-majority catchments (Kalyan, Baner) many households avoid non-veg on Mondays/Tuesdays/Thursdays/Saturdays - show a mild dip on one or two of those days (low confidence on magnitude).

Shravan + Ganeshotsav (biggest negative for a Maharashtra non-veg brand): Devyani blamed 'vegetarian days' (Sawan/Shravan, Ganpati) for KFC ADS falling from Rs 104k to Rs 96k (about -8% QoQ) in Q2 FY25 and said the effect is widening geographically; Sapphire KFC SSSG -3% partly on Navratri timing. Thane vendors sold 15-20 chickens/day during Ganeshotsav vs 50-60 on the Sunday after Anant Chaturdashi. Mock guidance: -10 to -20% in Kalyan/Baner, -5 to -10% in Bandra/Fort/Andheri, then a +20-30% rebound weekend right after visarjan. Dates (general knowledge, verify): Shravan (amanta) 25-Jul to 23-Aug-2025 and ~13-Aug to 11-Sep-2026; Ganesh Chaturthi 27-Aug-2025 and ~14-Sep-2026; Anant Chaturdashi 6-Sep-2025 and ~25-Sep-2026.

Navratri: nine days of reduced meat eating - another -5 to -15% dip (22-Sep to 1-Oct-2025; ~11-20 Oct-2026, verify). Paryushan and occasional civic meat-sale ban days also hurt (low confidence, not researched). Diwali week itself is weak for delivery QSR on the main day and strong on surrounding weekends (assumption).

Ramadan / Eid (positive for a Mughlai kebab brand): Swiggy saw +34% orders in the 5:30-7 pm iftar window, biryani +15% vs regular months, haleem ~15x, phirni/malpua +80%, with Mumbai among the top cities for iftar sweets. Pattern to mock: daytime lunch softer in Muslim-dominant catchments, sharp iftar spike, strong late-night/sehri orders, peak on Eid. Net month uplift +5-15% is my assumption. Dates (verify): Ramadan ~2-30 Mar-2025, ~19-Feb to 19-Mar-2026; Eid-ul-Fitr ~31-Mar-2025, ~20/21-Mar-2026; Bakri Eid ~27/28-May-2026.

Monsoon (June-September): heavy-rain days lift delivery orders 15-30% (one Mumbai operator reports +10-15%) and AOV 15-25%, while walk-ins fall; rider shortages cause longer delivery times and cancellations, and extreme waterlogging days can collapse both channels. Show higher aggregator share, more cancellations/refunds and soggy-packaging complaints in July-August; Petpooja walk-in sales down.

IPL (late March to end May): Swiggy IPL-2026 food orders +32% vs IPL-2025; peaks around 7:56-8:12 pm (5,200-6,200 orders/minute on playoff/final nights); Domino's/Pizza Hut reported +15-20% on match days; Mumbai among top-3 cities; chicken biryani and chicken snacks lead. Mock: +10-20% delivery on match evenings, bigger on weekends and Mumbai Indians games.
Month-end / salary cycle: no published data found. Assumption: days 1-10 of the month +5-8% and the last week -5-8%, stronger effect in Kalyan than Bandra. Low confidence.

Peak single days: New Year's Eve (Zomato reported NYE order volumes +45% YoY), Eid, IPL final, India cricket matches, first rain-heavy weekend. Trough days: Ganesh Chaturthi day, Anant Chaturdashi (road closures), Mahashivratri, Ashadhi Ekadashi, election/dry days (assumption).

Cost-side seasonality to mirror in the P&L: commercial LPG in Mumbai jumped from ~Rs 1,640 (Jan-2026) to ~Rs 3,070 (Jun-2026) and was ~Rs 2,700 in Sep-2026; chicken prices typically soften in Shravan (-4% to -25% in sources) and firm up right after; electricity peaks April-June and October (AC load); statutory bonus paid around Diwali; tomato/onion spikes in monsoon.
tax_notes: Restaurant service by a standalone outlet is taxed at 5% GST WITHOUT input tax credit (18% with ITC only for 'specified premises' - hotels with room tariff >= Rs 7,500). Miya Kebabs therefore cannot claim ITC on anything used for the restaurant business.

Consequence: every input GST becomes a P&L cost - 18% on rent, aggregator commission, payment-gateway fees and ads, POS/software, pest control, repairs, professional fees, commercial LPG and most packaging; 5-18% embedded in food inputs; 18% on capex (capitalise it into the asset cost and depreciate). Model these expense lines GROSS of GST. Example: Rs 1.4 L rent costs Rs 1.652 L; 23% commission costs 27.1%.

If the landlord is unregistered, the registered restaurant pays 18% on commercial rent under reverse charge (RCM) in cash - still no ITC, so the cost is identical but it shows up in GSTR-3B as an RCM liability.

Aggregator orders - Section 9(5) CGST (since 1-Jan-2022): Swiggy/Zomato are deemed suppliers, collect the 5% GST from the customer and pay it themselves. The restaurant does not charge or pay GST on these orders, does not receive that GST in its payout, and reports the taxable value in GSTR-3B Table 3.1.1(ii). GST TCS u/s 52 does not apply to these restaurant supplies (CBIC Circular 167/23/2021). So the mock's aggregator revenue must be shown net of GST, and 'GST payable' should arise only on Petpooja in-store/takeaway/own-delivery sales.

In-store (Petpooja) sales: outlet charges 5% GST (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST) and pays it fully in cash since no ITC is available to offset. A useful dashboard tile: GST liability = 5% x in-store net sales; aggregator sales = Rs 0 liability (paid by ECO).

TDS u/s 194-O: aggregators deduct 0.1% of GROSS sales (reduced from 1% w.e.f. 1-Oct-2024; 5% if no PAN). It is not an expense - it is a tax credit visible in Form 26AS, to be shown as 'TDS receivable' in payout reconciliation. (A secondary source indicates the provision is renumbered under the new Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1-Apr-2026 - verify with the client's CA.)

Payout reconciliation identity to respect in mock data: Net payout = order value (ex-GST, after restaurant-funded discount) - commission - PG fee - 18% GST on those fees - ads (+18% GST) - refund/complaint adjustments - TDS 0.1%. Settlements are typically weekly.

GST 2.0 (56th GST Council, effective 22-Sep-2025) cut rates on several food inputs (e.g. packaged paneer and Indian breads to nil; cheese, butter/ghee-type dairy, nuts, sauces to 5%) and raised aerated/sugary drinks to 40% - slightly lowers embedded tax in COGS after Sept-2025, raises cost of soft drinks sold. Restaurant output rate stays 5% without ITC. Local delivery services supplied through e-commerce operators were also brought under 9(5) at 18% - this affects the platforms' delivery fee, not the restaurant's P&L.

Electricity carries no GST but does carry Maharashtra electricity duty (21% for commercial per most sources; one site shows 16% - verify) and Tax on Sale of Electricity (34.04 paise/unit in Mumbai, 19.04 paise in MSEDCL city areas) - both are costs.

Factory/central kitchen: if it is the same legal entity and GSTIN, transfers to outlets are internal stock movements and the factory's input GST is likewise blocked (it is used for the 5%-without-ITC restaurant supply). If the factory were a separate entity selling to outlets, its sales would attract GST at product rates and the outlets still could not claim ITC - a structuring question for the client's CA; do not assert either structure in the mock.

Payroll compliance: EPF 12% employer (+~1% EDLI/admin) on wages up to Rs 15,000; ESIC 3.25% employer / 0.75% employee up to Rs 21,000 gross; Maharashtra minimum wages for Hotels & Restaurants revised half-yearly (Zone I from 1-Jul-2026: unskilled 14,676 / semi-skilled 15,176 / skilled 15,876); Labour Code wage definition (wages >= 50% of gross) applies from Nov/Dec-2025.

Net sales 20.00 (aggregator 12.00, in-store 8.00)
- Food/COGS 33%: 6.60
- Packaging (approx 3,160 delivery orders x Rs 16 + 3,200 in-store x Rs 7): 0.73 (3.6%)
=> Gross margin after food + packaging: 12.67 = 63.4%
- Aggregator costs: commission 23% 2.76 + PG 2% 0.24 + 18% GST on both 0.54 + ads 5% 0.60 + GST on ads 0.11 + refunds 0.8% 0.10 = 4.34 (21.7% of total sales; 36.2% of aggregator net sales; implies net realisation approx 57% of menu price after discount and packaging - inside the 52-62% 'healthy' band)
- Occupancy: rent 1.40 + 18% GST 0.25 + CAM 0.06 = 1.71 (8.6%)
- Utilities: electricity 0.32 + LPG 0.27 (10 cyl x Rs 2,701) + charcoal 0.15 + water 0.03 = 0.77 (3.8%)
- People: gross payroll 2.10 + PF/ESIC approx 15% 0.30 + bonus/gratuity accrual approx 10% 0.20 + staff meals 0.18 + accommodation 0.20 = 2.98 (14.9%)
- Other opex: consumables 0.12, local marketing 1.5% 0.30, R&M 1.5% 0.30, pest + waste 0.05, POS/internet/MDR 0.07, licences + insurance 0.05, petty cash 0.08, factory logistics 0.20 = 1.17 (5.9%)
Total costs 18.30 => Outlet EBITDA 1.70 = 8.5%. Depreciation approx 0.18 => EBIT approx 7.6%. Prime cost (food + people) = 47.9%, well under the 60-65% ceiling because aggregator fees, not labour, are the second-largest line.

Sensitivity with the same cost structure: at Rs 18 L net sales EBITDA approx 1.08 = 6.0%; at Rs 25 L approx 3.27 = 13.1% (rent and most labour fixed). 'Star outlet' case at Rs 22 L with 50% aggregator share, food 31%, commission 22%, ads 4%, discounts 8%: costs approx 18.07 => EBITDA approx 3.93 = 17.9%. Small-outlet case at Rs 10 L (70% aggregator, lean 6-7 staff, Kalyan rent 0.47 incl. GST): approx +1% i.e. break-even. The researcher's own check (break-even at Rs 15 L menu sales; 6-8% at Rs 20 L) reproduces within 1 point, so their arithmetic is sound; the only material understatement is employer statutory cost (approx 1 pt).

Verdict: plausible and consistent with listed peers (KFC India restaurant EBITDA 16.8-16.9%, Pizza Hut approx 0% to -3%), but typical-on-every-line lands at 6-13% for an Rs 18-25 L outlet, i.e. at or below the bottom of the 12-22% 'healthy' band. A believable 5-outlet portfolio: one star 16-18%, two or three at 9-14%, one marginal 2-6% (high rent/sales such as Fort at approx 15%, or heavy discounting). After factory under-absorption (if transfers are at raw-material cost, factory conversion approx 5-7% of brand sales - assumption) and HO overhead (approx 4-7% - assumption), company-level EBITDA of roughly 4-9% is the defensible range for the consolidated dashboard.
verify.notes:
WHAT STANDS (verified this session): Maharashtra Hotels & Restaurants minimum wages Jul-Dec 2026, Zone I 14,676 / 15,176 / 15,876 (basic 6,500/7,000/7,700 + special allowance 8,176) - exact match on WageIndicator; Mumbai, Pune and Kalyan-Dombivli are municipal corporations so Zone I applies. AEML and BEST LT-II(a) tariffs, fixed Rs 475, and AEML LT-III values - exact match in MERC press notes. MSEDCL LT-II values - exact match in the fresh 25-Mar-2026 order. Commercial LPG history - two sources agree. C&W main-street rents - exact match. Aggregator economics: commission 18-28%, PG approx 2%, 18% GST on fees, ads 4-9% for active bidders, packaging Rs 8-22/order, net realisation 52-62% healthy / under 50% loss-making, RestaurantDaily worked examples (Rs 500 order -> Rs 161 net; Rs 8 L GMV month -> 53.5%) - all reproduced from the cited pages. Food cost 28-35% with >38% red flag - confirmed (Petpooja blog, DineOpen). TDS 194-O 0.1% from 1-Oct-2024 and s.9(5) treatment - confirmed (HelloBooks). DineOpen cost-benchmark table (labour 20-30, rent 8-15, utilities 3-5, marketing 2-5, repairs 1-2, misc 3-5) and the Bandra vs Jaipur rent example - confirmed as quoted, but it is a vendor blog. UPI MDR from 15-Oct-2026 - confirmed via Business Today only.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED (treat as assumption / low confidence): Tata Power LT-II numbers; electricity duty 21%; FAC magnitudes; PNG commercial Rs 60/SCM; Glassdoor manager pay, WorkIndia/Quikr cook postings (403 or not re-fetched) - ranges are nonetheless plausible against the minimum-wage floor; all lines the researcher marked ASSUMPTION; factory staffing and cost; Zomato long-distance-fee cap; FSSAI April-2026 changes; Sapphire KFC gross margin.

GUIDANCE FOR THE MOCK (unit-economics screens): (1) Show aggregator cost lines only as they appear in payout statements - commission, PG/collection fee, GST on fees, ads, long-distance fee (Zomato only), refund/complaint adjustments, TDS as receivable - with rates labelled as configurable contract rates. (2) Never show customer-paid delivery fee, platform fee, tips or aggregator-order GST inside outlet revenue or cost. (3) Model rent, aggregator fees, POS, pest control, LPG gross of 18% GST (5%-without-ITC restaurant). (4) Keep electricity as kWh x configurable all-in rate (Mumbai approx Rs 10.1-10.9; Kalyan/Pune approx Rs 12.5-13.3) and LPG as cylinders x monthly price so the 2026 LPG spike flows through automatically. (5) Put an 'illustrative assumption' tag on every unsourced line and on all factory figures. (6) Decide and document the factory transfer-price convention before generating data. (7) Tune per-outlet levers (aggregator share, discount depth, rent/sales, food cost) rather than using typical values everywhere, to land a portfolio of roughly 17% / 9-14% / 2-6% outlet EBITDA.
